meta.purpose: Trusted-source registry for the personal-learning green card questionnaire tool. Each source lists which rulebook.json field paths it can authoritatively update, so the freshness agent knows which source to hit for which field. Tier 1 = official government primary sources. Tier 2 = law firm aggregators and trackers. Tier 3 = community sources for sanity checks only, never authoritative.
meta.scope_note: This registry covers only the monthly-cadence fields the freshness agent touches (bulletin dates, USCIS processing times, DOL queue positions, wait-band estimates). It intentionally does NOT list sources for rules-that-don't-move (CFR citations, AC21 provisions, MSA definitions, case names) — those are baked into rulebook.json permanently and never refreshed by the agent.

tier_1_primary.name: U.S. Department of State — Visa Bulletin
tier_1_primary.access_notes: DOS frequently 403-blocks direct HTTP fetches from non-browser user agents. When fetch fails, fall back to tier-2 aggregators and require agreement across at least two aggregators before accepting the value. Do NOT trust a single tier-2 source alone when tier-1 is unavailable.

tier_1_primary.name: USCIS — Case Processing Times
tier_1_primary.access_notes: HUMAN-ONLY — CANNOT AUTO-FETCH. egov.uscis.gov sits behind a Cloudflare 'Verify you are human' bot challenge (interactive checkbox). Verified 2026-08-05: WebFetch returns HTTP 403; a headless browser (Playwright) loads only the Cloudflare 'Performing security verification' interstitial, never the data. Defeating the challenge would be circumventing a federal site's access controls (out of bounds). The freshness agent MUST NOT attempt to fetch this source. Treatment in the tool: link the user out to this page rather than hardcoding a processing-time number. Processing-time values are also the lowest-leverage data in the tool (an 8-vs-11-month I-140 is noise against a 15-year EB-2 India priority-date wait), so a stale hardcoded value is worse than a live link.

tier_1_primary.name: USCIS — Form Fee Schedule (Form I-907 Premium Processing)
tier_1_primary.access_notes: Fee changes only when USCIS publishes a Federal Register rule. Cadence is effectively yearly or less; agent should treat 'no change' as the default and flag any change hard.

tier_1_primary.name: U.S. Department of Labor — FLAG PERM Disclosure Data
tier_1_primary.access_notes: Bulk quarterly CSV / dashboard. DOL publishes lag-corrected queue-position updates on its own cadence; the FAQ page in the OFLC PERM Processing Times section carries the human-readable 'we are currently processing filings from month X' string.

tier_1_primary.name: U.S. Department of Labor — OFLC Processing Times
tier_1_primary.access_notes: Companion to FLAG for the queue-position narrative. Cross-check the 'currently processing filings from X' string against flag.dol.gov before accepting.

tier_1_primary.name: eCFR — 20 CFR Part 656 (PERM regulations)
tier_1_primary.access_notes: Rules-that-don't-move source. Referenced by rulebook for citation strings only. NOT touched by the freshness agent — if this changes, the change is a legislative or rulemaking event that requires human review of the entire rulebook, not a monthly refresh.

tier_1_primary.name: eCFR — 8 CFR Part 214 (H-1B nonimmigrant regulations)
tier_1_primary.access_notes: Rules-that-don't-move. Freshness agent must NOT touch fields citing this source.

tier_1_primary.name: eCFR — 8 CFR Part 204 (immigrant petition regulations)
tier_1_primary.access_notes: Rules-that-don't-move. Freshness agent must NOT touch fields citing this source.

tier_1_primary.name: USCIS Policy Manual
tier_1_primary.access_notes: Rules and policy interpretations (e.g. Matter of Dhanasar for EB-2 NIW). Not a monthly-refresh source. Structural changes require full-rulebook review.

tier_1_primary.name: U.S. Census Bureau — Metropolitan and Micropolitan Statistical Areas
tier_1_primary.access_notes: MSA delineations. Census updates these on a multi-year cycle. NOT touched by the freshness agent — a Census MSA revision is a rulebook-wide review event, not a monthly refresh.

tier_1_primary.name: U.S. Congress — American Competitiveness in the 21st Century Act (Pub. L. 106-313)
tier_1_primary.access_notes: Statute. Not touched by the freshness agent. Only relevant if Congress amends AC21, which is a legislative event.

tier_2_aggregators.name: Murthy Law Firm — Visa Bulletin analysis
tier_2_aggregators.access_notes: Republishes the DOS Visa Bulletin with plain-language commentary. Reliably fetches. Cross-check numbers against a second aggregator before accepting when DOS is 403-blocked.

tier_2_aggregators.name: Fragomen — Visa Bulletin summaries
tier_2_aggregators.access_notes: Large-firm client alerts. Coverage is consistent for the top EB categories and generally posts within 48 hours of the DOS release. Good second tier-2 source to cross-check Murthy.

tier_2_aggregators.name: Boundless — Visa Bulletin explainer
tier_2_aggregators.access_notes: Consumer-focused platform. Chart-note (which chart USCIS honors) is often surfaced clearly. Less reliable for less-common categories.

tier_2_aggregators.name: Morgan Lewis — Immigration client alerts
tier_2_aggregators.access_notes: Cited by rulebook wait-estimate bands for EB-1 India. Publishes structural analysis alongside monthly numbers.

tier_2_aggregators.name: Green Card Clock — priority-date and wait-band tracker
tier_2_aggregators.access_notes: Community-driven tracker aggregating bulletin history plus wait-time models. Reliable for structural wait-band context; treat point-in-time date claims as tier-2 (cross-check).

tier_2_aggregators.name: USA Visa Law — Visa Bulletin coverage
tier_2_aggregators.access_notes: Cited by rulebook wait-estimate bands. Consistent monthly Visa Bulletin summaries.

tier_3_community.name: Trackitt — PERM and I-140 case tracker
tier_3_community.access_notes: Anonymous user-reported case timeline data. Skew: heavily India-cohort, self-selected reporters. Use for directional sanity check only; never accept a Trackitt value as authoritative.

tier_3_community.name: Reddit — r/immigration and r/USCIS
tier_3_community.access_notes: Anecdotal discussion. Never authoritative. Only useful for detecting that something changed (e.g. USCIS quietly updated a policy) before tier-1 catches up. Any Reddit-sourced claim must be independently verified against a tier-1 source before it is proposed as a rulebook update.
